samplingProtocol.producerIncludes: record calls, producer instrumentation, flush calls, I/O during awaits, and cadence waits
samplingProtocol.eventLoopWindow: delay histogram includes post-reset arming until first sample (20 ms polling, 1 s timeout) and 20 ms tail observation, plus baseline GC through final GC; includes nominal timer interval, not only excess delay; ELU excludes arm and tail
samplingProtocol.workloadWindow: first producer action through close completion; excludes setup, input allocation, final GC and inspect
samplingProtocol.normalization: verified raw digests; top-level runId to same-length zero UUID, generated startedAt/updatedAt to fixed ISO time; derived status/inspect digests mapped to normalized trace digests; event objects unchanged

primaryOrder: 27 baseline workers followed by 27 candidate workers; 9 scenarios, 3 repeats each

formulas.percentChange: 100 * delta / baseline; null for zero/missing baseline
formulas.aggregation: median/min/max of paired observations; percent medians are not ratios of medians

limitations: Three descriptive repeats per scenario/group; no significance or general performance claim.
Raw bytes differ due to run UUIDs/timestamps; only declared identities, generated times, inspect.runDir and verified trace-derived hashes are normalized.
Sustained workload is a bounded 500-round run around 20 seconds, not a long-running soak.
Process CPU includes all process threads and instrumentation; short Windows windows show quantized values.
ELU is not CPU utilization; the delay histogram includes arming/tail observation intervals.
Memory growth includes retained measurement samples, rounds and latency arrays; not proof of a recorder leak.
Initial sustained CPU rose; interleaved CPU results remain mixed. No CPU saving conclusion.
